summary: How people and systems get something done: an operational, business or engineering process (onboarding, month-end close, incident response, release, approval flow...).

purpose.must: Why the process exists, what triggers it (event, date, request), what its outcome is and how one knows it finished well.

scope.must: When it applies and when it does not (in scope / out of scope), frequency and volume, which areas, products or regions are covered.

skeleton.pt-BR:
| Dentro do escopo | Fora do escopo |
| --- | --- |
| «…» | «…» |

«Frequência, volume e áreas cobertas.»
skeleton.en:
| In scope | Out of scope |
| --- | --- |
| «…» | «…» |

«Frequency, volume and areas covered.»

roles.must: Every role that acts in the process, its responsibility and who holds it today (team or person as given by the sources).

steps.must: Every step in order: owner (a role from Roles, same name), input, output, system/tool, deadline/SLA. '—' only when the sources say there is none; when nobody knows, write 'Em aberto (ver Perguntas em aberto)' / 'Open (see Open questions)' and add the question. Conditional paths (e.g. approval tiers by value) are one row per branch with the condition in the step name, or a decision step plus rows; say when the order (sequential or parallel) is unknown. One collapsible block per complex step with detailed instructions.

raci.must: Rows = the steps from Steps (same names or numbers), columns = the roles from Roles (same names). Cells: R, A, C, I or combinations like R/A; '—' means the sources state no participation. Exactly one A per step: when the sources name only who performs a step, mark the performer R/A and add an open question about accountability.

systems-tools.must: Every system, spreadsheet, form or tool used, in which steps, for what, and how access is obtained.

exceptions.must: What can go wrong at each step, the alternative path, who decides, escalation chain and contacts (roles), what to do when the deadline is missed.

sla-metrics.must: SLAs and KPIs with exact definitions, targets, data source and who tracks them.

controls.must: Approvals, segregation of duties, evidence kept (what, where, for how long), audits, regulations or policies the process satisfies.

skeleton.pt-BR:
| Controle | Evidência | Onde fica | Por quanto tempo | Fonte |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| «…» | «…» | «…» | «…» | «…» |
skeleton.en:
| Control | Evidence | Where it is kept | Retention | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| «…» | «…» | «…» | «…» | «…» |

artifacts.must: Documents, forms, templates and records produced or consumed, with where they live.

skeleton.pt-BR:
| Documento / modelo | Produzido ou usado em | Onde fica |
| --- | --- | --- |
| «…» | «…» | «…» |
skeleton.en:
| Document / template | Produced or used in | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| «…» | «…» | «…» |

summary.must: Card grid (4-10 cards): goal, trigger, frequency, owner, average duration, main system, current status. Close with an 'In one sentence:' line.

flow.must: Mermaid flowchart (or sequence diagram with roles as participants) of the main path and the main decision points, then numbered prose walking through it.

status.must: The first sentence carries the date. Maturity (ad hoc, documented, measured, automated), last review, known pain points, planned changes.

business-rules.must: Every rule the process must respect (limits, approvals by value, deadlines, eligibility), with its source (policy, regulation, decision).

risks.must: Risk, impact, severity, mitigation. Includes single points of failure (one person holds a role), manual steps prone to error, missing controls.

references.must: Every source this document was built from: the documents, links, transcripts and people interviewed (with date) listed in the front matter `sources`, plus how the document is maintained.

crossref.message: every role in Roles must be a column of the RACI matrix
every step owner must be a role listed in Roles (same name)
